task.description: Observed twice on 2026-10-28 while two agent tool calls ran storypole mutations in parallel: the ledger gained a line holding two concatenated JSON objects and every subsequent command failed with 'Corrupt ledger at line N: trailing characters at line 1 column M'. Incidents were at line 747 (claim + three defers) and line 833 (decide + claim). Appends are not atomic against concurrent writers: there is no advisory lock and no guarantee the event is written in a single syscall, so interleaved writers splice objects. Repair requires hand-splitting the affected line and deleting index.sqlite, because the SQLite projection does not notice an externally repaired ledger. Desired: take an advisory lock (flock) or write via a single serialized append per event; add an integrity check that refuses to append to a corrupt tail; and invalidate/rebuild the index when the ledger mtime or size no longer matches the projection.
task.title: Concurrent storypole invocations corrupt the ledger by splicing two JSON events onto one line

receipt.summary: Merged to storypole main (0c9c0be): append_event now serialises the event into one buffer and writes it with a single append instead of a formatted writeln!, which could issue several writes and interleave with a concurrent writer. A tail check refuses to append to a ledger whose last byte is not a newline, returning CorruptLedger rather than swallowing an event, and the index is unaffected. Regression tests: 8 concurrent writers x 20 events produce exactly 160 lines, every one valid JSON and fully replayable; the corrupt-tail refusal leaves the file untouched; empty/missing file still works. Gates: clippy -p storypole-core --all-targets -D warnings clean, nextest -p storypole-core 28/28, fmt and docs clean.
